concepts.name: Sharing private files with content URI grants
Auto Backup exclusions for private app files
Persisting photo-picker access for background work

questions.prompt: An Android app shares a private PDF with another app using FileProvider. How should it give the recipient read access?

choices.text: Send the private file path and request broad storage permission
Send the content URI with a temporary read-URI permission flag
Replace the content URI with a file URI to bypass access checks
Mark the PDF directory world-readable before sending its path

questions.explanation: FileProvider content URIs plus FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION grant scoped temporary access. A private raw path is not a grant; file URIs and world-readable storage bypass the documented secure-sharing design.

sources.title: Sharing a file
sources.claim: FileProvider creates content URIs for configured paths; an Intent read-URI grant gives the receiving app temporary access without exposing a raw file URI or granting broad storage access.

questions.prompt: A device-specific secret must not be included in Android Auto Backup. Which directory is specifically intended for files excluded from that backup?

choices.text: The directory returned by `getNoBackupFilesDir()`
The shared-preferences directory without custom backup rules
The directory returned by `getFilesDir()` without custom rules
The database directory without any custom backup exclusion rules

questions.explanation: Auto Backup excludes getNoBackupFilesDir. Internal files, databases and shared preferences are normally included, so putting the secret there without exclusions does not meet this requirement.

sources.title: Back up user data with Auto Backup
sources.claim: Auto Backup normally includes shared preferences, internal files and databases, but excludes cache, code-cache and getNoBackupFilesDir directories; rules can exclude particular files.

questions.prompt: An Android app selects a video through the photo picker and queues a background upload that may run after the app stops. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Default picker access can end when the app stops or the device restarts
Photo selection automatically grants read access to the entire library
Persist the selected URI read grant with `takePersistableUriPermission`
The picker provides scoped access to user-selected media files
A stored URI string alone guarantees read access after the app stops

questions.explanation: Persisting the read grant supports longer-running work. The picker grants selected-media access rather than whole-library permission. Default access has a limited lifetime; storing the URI text does not preserve the permission itself.

sources.title: Photo picker
sources.claim: Photo picker grants access to selected media rather than the entire library; takePersistableUriPermission with a read flag extends access for long-running background work.

questions.prompt: Why use a FileProvider content URI rather than a raw private file path for an Android share operation?

choices.text: It permanently gives every installed app access to that file
It supports a temporary grant to the particular receiving app
It makes the whole internal storage directory public to all apps
It removes the need to configure which file paths can be shared

questions.explanation: The content URI lets Android enforce a recipient-specific temporary grant. FileProvider still needs configured shareable paths; it does not expose all internal storage or grant permanent universal access.

sources.title: Sharing a file
sources.claim: FileProvider creates content URIs for configured paths; an Intent read-URI grant gives the receiving app temporary access without exposing a raw file URI or granting broad storage access.

questions.prompt: An Android developer stores a critical restore token only in `getCacheDir()` and relies on default Auto Backup. What is the flaw?

choices.text: Cache directories are included whenever the token is small
Cache directories are backed up before shared preferences
Cache directories are backed up only when the app is stopped
Cache directories are excluded from Auto Backup

questions.explanation: Auto Backup excludes cache and code-cache directories irrespective of token size. Backup ordering or stopping the app does not turn a cache file into backed-up persistent data.

sources.title: Back up user data with Auto Backup
sources.claim: Auto Backup normally includes shared preferences, internal files and databases, but excludes cache, code-cache and getNoBackupFilesDir directories; rules can exclude particular files.

questions.prompt: An Android app needs to upload photo-picker media after the app stops. Which choices preserve the relevant permission correctly? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Assume a WorkManager network constraint preserves the URI grant
Call `takePersistableUriPermission` on the selected URI
Treat a saved URI string as a permanent replacement for a permission
Use `FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION` for persisted read access
Read the media once to make the temporary grant automatically permanent

questions.explanation: Persist the URI permission with ContentResolver.takePersistableUriPermission and the read flag. Saving a string, adding constraints or reading once does not extend the temporary grant.

sources.title: Photo picker
sources.claim: Photo picker grants access to selected media rather than the entire library; takePersistableUriPermission with a read flag extends access for long-running background work.
